kabsa.name: Kabsa
kabsa.summary: Arab mixed rice dish originating from Saudi Arabia or Yemen, widely regarded as a national dish across Gulf Cooperation Council countries.

malabar-coast.name: Malabar Coast
malabar-coast.summary: Southwestern coastal region of India stretching from Konkan to Kanyakumari, one of the subcontinent's wettest and most biodiverse areas.

arabic-coffee.name: Arabic coffee (qahwa)
arabic-coffee.summary: Bitter coffee brewed across Arab countries, often spiced with cardamom, originating in Yemen's port of Mokha and traditionally served to guests as a sign of hospitality.

manti-food.name: Manti
manti-food.summary: A dumpling dish of spiced meat wrapped in dough, found across Central Asia, West Asia, the South Caucasus and the Balkans, and especially popular in Turkish cuisine.

strained-yogurt.name: Labneh
strained-yogurt.summary: A strained yogurt even thicker than Greek yogurt, made by removing most of the whey, widely eaten across the Middle East and Central Asia.

sobia.name: Sobia
sobia.summary: A cold drink popular in Egypt and Saudi Arabia; the Saudi version is a fermented mix of wheat flour, malt, sugar and spices, especially drunk during Ramadan.

hejaz.name: Hejaz
hejaz.summary: A historical region of western Arabia, in modern Saudi Arabia, containing the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, the first and second holiest sites in Islam.

abdulhalim-radwi.name: Abdulhalim Radwi
abdulhalim-radwi.summary: Saudi painter and sculptor (1939–2006), trained in Rome and Madrid, who taught art in Riyadh and led cultural institutions in Jeddah.

saud-of-saudi-arabia.name: King Saud
saud-of-saudi-arabia.summary: King of Saudi Arabia from 1953 until his 1964 abdication, and the country's second king; earlier he was crown prince from 1933 and helped establish the state's first budget and central bank.

ijazah.name: Ijazah
ijazah.summary: A license authorizing someone to teach a text or subject, especially Islamic religious knowledge, granted by a holder of that same authority; some scholars link it to the origin of academic degrees.

safeya-binzagr.name: Safeya Binzagr
safeya-binzagr.summary: A Saudi Arabian artist (1940-2024) active in Jeddah's art scene, who opened her own museum and gallery, the Darat Safeya Binzagr, in 2000, the only artist in her country to have one.

munira-mosli.name: Munira Mosli
munira-mosli.summary: Saudi Arabian plastic works artist and painter (1954–2019) who worked with copper, natural dyes, palm fibre, paper and other materials using collage techniques; a Saudi art gallery was later renamed in her honor.

accademia-di-belle-arti-di-roma.name: Accademia di Belle Arti di Roma
accademia-di-belle-arti-di-roma.summary: A public art academy in Rome founded in the 16th century, with the present institution dating from Italy's unification in 1870.
accademia-di-belle-arti-di-roma.source_title: Accademia di Belle Arti di Roma

ibn-saud.name: Ibn Saud
ibn-saud.summary: Najdi war leader and statesman who founded Saudi Arabia, reigning as king from 1932 until his death in 1953; he had ruled parts of the region since retaking Riyadh in 1902.

rashidi-dynasty.name: Rashidi dynasty
rashidi-dynasty.summary: Arabian dynasty (1836–1921) that ruled the Emirate of Ha'il and was the House of Saud's fiercest rival, until defeated by Abdulaziz Al Saud in 1921.

najd.name: Najd
najd.summary: A historical central region of the Arabian Peninsula, home to about a third of Saudi Arabia's population and to the House of Saud.

al-ahsa-governorate.name: Al-Ahsa
al-ahsa-governorate.summary: A governorate in eastern Saudi Arabia, historically called Hajar, the largest in the country by area, with Hofuf as its seat.

emirate-of-jabal-shammar.name: Jabal Shammar
emirate-of-jabal-shammar.summary: A state in the northern Arabian Peninsula centered on Ha'il, ruled by the Rashidi dynasty from the mid-19th century until 1921, covering parts of modern Saudi Arabia, Iraq and Jordan.

yahya-muhammad-hamid-ed-din.name: Imam Yahya
yahya-muhammad-hamid-ed-din.summary: First king of the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen (1918–1948) and Zaydi imam, who fought to expel Ottoman rule and kept his isolated kingdom largely closed to the outside world.

najran.name: Najran
najran.summary: A city in southwestern Saudi Arabia, an ancient trade and agricultural center on caravan routes, notable for its pre-Islamic Christian community.

khafji.name: Khafji
khafji.summary: A city in eastern Saudi Arabia near the border with Kuwait.

saudi-arabian-national-guard.name: Saudi Arabian National Guard
saudi-arabian-national-guard.summary: One of three branches of the Saudi Arabian military, made up of tribal fighters loyal to the House of Saud and tasked with protecting the royal family, including from coups.

prince-sultan-air-base.name: Prince Sultan Air Base
prince-sultan-air-base.summary: A Saudi Arabian military air base in Al Kharj, named after former defense minister and Crown Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Al Saud.

ras-tanura.name: Ras Tanura
ras-tanura.summary: Industrial port city and governorate in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, on a peninsula known for its major oil refinery.

kingdom-of-hejaz.name: Kingdom of Hejaz
kingdom-of-hejaz.summary: A short-lived Hashemite-ruled state in western Arabia proclaimed independent of the Ottomans in 1916 during the Arab Revolt, before its 1924–25 conquest by Saudi forces.

alexei-vasiliev-historian.name: Alexei Vasiliev
alexei-vasiliev-historian.summary: A Russian historian specializing in Arab and African studies, who directed the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute for African Studies from 1992 to 2015 and later became its honorary president.

aden.name: Aden
aden.summary: Ancient port city on Yemen's south coast, at the eastern approach to the Red Sea, serving since 2014 as the de facto capital of Yemen's internationally recognized government.

taif.name: Taif
taif.summary: A city in the Hejaz mountains of Saudi Arabia, visited by the Prophet Muhammad in the early 7th century and long inhabited by the Banu Thaqif tribe.

suroor.name: Mohammed Suroor Sabban
suroor.summary: Saudi Arabian politician, economist, publisher and poet who lived from 1898 to 1971.

cities-of-salt.name: Cities of Salt
cities-of-salt.summary: A 1984 novel by Abdul Rahman Munif depicting the transformation of an Arabian oasis after the discovery of oil, recognized as a major work of Arab literature.

abdul-rahman-munif.name: Abdul Rahman Munif
abdul-rahman-munif.summary: Saudi-born novelist and cultural critic (1933–2004), among the most significant 20th-century Arabic authors, best known for the Cities of Salt quintet; his Saudi citizenship was revoked after his books offended its rulers.

mahmoud-darwish.name: Mahmoud Darwish
mahmoud-darwish.summary: Palestinian author and poet (1941-2008) who wrote the Palestinian Declaration of Independence and is widely regarded as the country's national poet.

riyadh-international-book-fair.name: Riyadh Book Fair
riyadh-international-book-fair.summary: An annual 11-day book fair in Saudi Arabia drawing over half a million visitors, often a flashpoint for political debate, with clashes between speakers, protestors and the religious police.

mohammed-suroor-sabban.name: Mohammed Suroor Sabban
mohammed-suroor-sabban.summary: A Saudi politician, economist, publisher, and poet from Qunfodah, who lived from 1898 to 1972.

qatif.name: Qatif
qatif.summary: One of the oldest settlements in Arabia, with a history dating to 3500 BC, historically known to the Sumerians as Dilmun and now part of Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province.

million-s-poet.name: Million's Poet
million-s-poet.summary: A reality television show in the United Arab Emirates, first broadcast in 2006, featuring a competition in composing and reciting Nabati vernacular poetry.

ousha-the-poet.name: Ousha bint Khalifa Al Suwaidi
ousha-the-poet.summary: An Emirati poet (1920–2018), also known as Fatat Al-Arab, regarded as among the finest Arabic Nabati poets.

wilfred-thesiger.name: Wilfred Thesiger
wilfred-thesiger.summary: British explorer and writer (1910–2003) known for crossing Arabia's Empty Quarter by foot and camel and for living among the Marsh Arabs of Iraq.

arabian-sands.name: Arabian Sands
arabian-sands.summary: A 1959 book by explorer Wilfred Thesiger recounting his 1945-1950 travels in Arabia, including two crossings of the Empty Quarter, and the Bedu way of life.

rub-al-khali.name: Empty Quarter
rub-al-khali.summary: A vast desert covering roughly 650,000 square kilometers across the southern Arabian Peninsula, spanning parts of Saudi Arabia, Oman, the UAE and Yemen.

muhammad-hasan-awwad.name: Muhammad Hasan Awwad
muhammad-hasan-awwad.summary: A Saudi author and thinker (1902–1980) from Hejaz, seen as a leader of early Saudi literature and philosophy and an advocate of modernization.

saqr-bin-sultan-al-qasimi.name: Saqr bin Sultan Al Qasimi
saqr-bin-sultan-al-qasimi.summary: Ruler of the Emirate of Sharjah from 1951 to 1965 who was removed in a coup, then returned from exile in 1972 in a failed coup attempt that led to his successor's murder.

king-abdullah-university-of-science-and-.name: KAUST
king-abdullah-university-of-science-and-.summary: A public research university in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia, founded in 2009 as the country's first mixed-gender university campus, teaching in English.
king-abdullah-university-of-science-and-.source_title: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

thuwal.name: Thuwal
thuwal.summary: A coastal village in Saudi Arabia's Hejaz region, home to the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, founded in 2009 as the country's first mixed-gender university campus.

arabian-oryx.name: Arabian oryx
arabian-oryx.summary: A desert antelope native to the Arabian Peninsula, hunted to extinction in the wild by the early 1970s and reintroduced from captive-bred animals starting in 1980.

san-diego-zoo-safari-park.name: San Diego Wild Animal Park
san-diego-zoo-safari-park.summary: Former name (until 2010) of the San Diego Zoo Safari Park, a California zoo and safari park opened in 1972 that focuses on animals from arid environments.

hok-firm.name: HOK
hok-firm.summary: An American design, architecture, engineering and urban planning firm founded in 1955 and headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri.

king-abdulaziz-city-for-science-and-tech.name: KACST
king-abdulaziz-city-for-science-and-tech.summary: A Saudi Arabian government science and technology organization established in 1977 and renamed King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology in 1985.
king-abdulaziz-city-for-science-and-tech.source_title: King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology

arabsat-6a.name: Arabsat-6A
arabsat-6a.summary: A geostationary communications satellite built by Lockheed Martin and launched aboard a Falcon Heavy rocket from Kennedy Space Center in April 2019.

iucn-red-list.name: IUCN Red List
iucn-red-list.summary: A global inventory, founded in 1964, of species' conservation status and extinction risk, used to guide conservation policy and action worldwide.

cites.name: CITES Appendix I
cites.summary: The highest protection category of CITES, a 1975 treaty regulating international trade in endangered species, restricting trade for species most at risk.

nature-index.name: Nature Index
nature-index.summary: A database launched in 2014 that tracks scientific output of institutions and countries by counting articles in leading journals, producing annual rankings including of fast-rising universities.

al-wusta-wildlife-reserve.name: Al Wusta Wildlife Reserve
al-wusta-wildlife-reserve.summary: A nature reserve in Oman's central desert, formerly the Arabian Oryx Sanctuary, and the first site ever removed from the UNESCO World Heritage List, in 2007, after its area was reduced for oil prospecting.

third-saudi-state.name: Third Saudi state
third-saudi-state.summary: The current Saudi state, begun in 1902 when Ibn Saud captured Riyadh; it passed through the Emirate of Riyadh, the Sultanate of Nejd and the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd before becoming the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in 1932.

hussein-king-of-hejaz.name: Hussein bin Ali
hussein-king-of-hejaz.summary: Sharif and Emir of Mecca from 1908 who launched the Great Arab Revolt against the Ottomans and became King of the Hejaz from 1916 to 1924.

sharif-of-mecca.name: Sharif of Mecca
sharif-of-mecca.summary: The title of the traditional steward of Mecca and Medina, charged with protecting the cities and pilgrims, an office dating back to the late Abbasid era into the 20th century.

house-of-saud.name: House of Saud
house-of-saud.summary: The ruling royal family of Saudi Arabia, descended from Muhammad bin Saud, founder of the 18th-century Emirate of Diriyah, and today among the wealthiest families in the world.

fahd-of-saudi-arabia.name: Fahd
fahd-of-saudi-arabia.summary: King and prime minister of Saudi Arabia from 1982 until his death in 2005, having earlier served as education and interior minister and as crown prince from 1975.

abdullah-of-saudi-arabia.name: Abdullah of Saudi Arabia
abdullah-of-saudi-arabia.summary: King and prime minister of Saudi Arabia from 2005 until his death in 2015, previously crown prince and de facto ruler after King Fahd's 1995 stroke; tenth son of the kingdom's founder.

consultative-assembly-of-saudi-arabia.name: Shura Council
consultative-assembly-of-saudi-arabia.summary: Saudi Arabia's appointed advisory body, which reviews laws and policy, examines government reports, and can summon ministers, with its recommendations passed on to the Prime Minister.

saud-bin-abdulaziz-al-rashid.name: Saud bin Abdulaziz Al Rashid
saud-bin-abdulaziz-al-rashid.summary: Tenth Emir of Jabal Shammar, who ruled between 1908 and 1920 (1898–1920).

kingdom-of-yemen.name: Kingdom of Yemen
kingdom-of-yemen.summary: The Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen, a state from 1918 to 1970 in northwestern Yemen led by Zaidi religious leaders (imams) starting with Imam Yahya, ending after a 1962 republican coup.

asir.name: Asir
asir.summary: A province in southern Saudi Arabia bordering Yemen, with Abha as its capital and a population of about 2 million.

hodeidah.name: Hodeidah
hodeidah.summary: The fourth-largest city in Yemen and its main port on the Red Sea, with a population of about 735,000 as of 2023.

abdullah-al-sallal.name: Abdullah al-Sallal
abdullah-al-sallal.summary: Yemeni military officer who led the 1962 North Yemeni Revolution and served as the Yemen Arab Republic's first president until 1967; his government abolished slavery.

yemen-arab-republic.name: Yemen Arab Republic
yemen-arab-republic.summary: A country in northwestern Yemen also known as North Yemen, formed after a 1962 republican coup and eight-year civil war, until unifying with South Yemen in 1990.

gamal-abdel-nasser.name: Gamal Abdel Nasser
gamal-abdel-nasser.summary: Egypt's second president (1954–1970), who led the 1952 revolution, nationalized the Suez Canal, championed pan-Arab unity, and briefly united Egypt and Syria in the United Arab Republic.

faisal-of-saudi-arabia.name: King Faisal
faisal-of-saudi-arabia.summary: King of Saudi Arabia from 1964 until his assassination in 1975, previously crown prince and long-serving prime minister who outlawed slavery and pursued modernization.

faisal-bin-musaid-al-saud.name: Faisal bin Musaid
faisal-bin-musaid-al-saud.summary: Nephew of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia who shot and killed him in March 1975 and was executed by beheading that June.

madawi-al-rasheed.name: Madawi al-Rasheed
madawi-al-rasheed.summary: British-Saudi professor of social anthropology, born 1962, granddaughter of the last prince of the Emirate of Ha'il, who writes on the Arabian Peninsula and Saudi politics.

saudi-philosophy-association.name: Saudi Philosophy Association
saudi-philosophy-association.summary: A non-profit association concerned with philosophy in Saudi Arabia, established in November 2020 as the country's first philosophical association.

abu-abd-al-rahman-ibn-aqil-al-zahiri.name: Ibn Aqil al-Zahiri
abu-abd-al-rahman-ibn-aqil-al-zahiri.summary: Saudi polymath called theologian, jurist, historian, ethnographer, geographer, poet, critic and author, and a member of Saudi Arabia's 'Golden Generation.'
abu-abd-al-rahman-ibn-aqil-al-zahiri.source_title: Abu Abd al-Rahman Ibn Aqil al-Zahiri

shaqra-saudi-arabia.name: Shaqra
shaqra-saudi-arabia.summary: A governorate in Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia, whose territory includes the city of Ushaiger, ancestral home of Qatar's ruling family.

salafi-movement.name: Salafism
salafi-movement.summary: A religious movement, emerging in the late 19th century, that calls for a return to the practices of the earliest generations of Muslims and has influenced many thinkers and movements across the Islamic world.

wahhabism.name: Wahhabism
wahhabism.summary: A Salafi revivalist movement within Sunni Islam named after the 18th-century scholar Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, originating in Najd and later spreading across the Arabian Peninsula.

zahiri-school.name: Zahiri school
zahiri-school.summary: A school of Sunni Islamic jurisprudence emphasizing the literal, apparent meaning of the Quran and Sunnah; it flourished in Islamic Spain under Ibn Hazm.

ibn-hazm.name: Ibn Hazm
ibn-hazm.summary: An Andalusian polymath, jurist and theologian (994–1064) from Córdoba, a leading codifier of the Zahiri legal school and one of the era's foremost thinkers.

al-uthaymin.name: Muhammad ibn al-Uthaymin
al-uthaymin.summary: A Saudi Islamic scholar (1929–2001), commonly known as Ibn Uthaymin.

ibn-baz.name: Ibn Baz
ibn-baz.summary: Saudi Arabia's Grand Mufti from 1993 until his death in 1999, who authorised a fatwa for a wealth tax for the mujahideen and whose endorsement of a book calling for jihad helped drive the war against the Soviet Union.

yusuf-al-qaradawi.name: Yusuf al-Qaradawi
yusuf-al-qaradawi.summary: Egyptian Islamic scholar (1926–2022) based in Qatar, known for his Al Jazeera programme 'Sharia and Life' and a prominent role in the Muslim Brotherhood's intellectual leadership.

averroes.name: Averroes (Ibn Rushd)
averroes.summary: Ibn Rushd (1126–1198), known in the West as Averroes, was an Andalusian polymath and jurist whose commentaries on Aristotle and defence of philosophy within Islam made him influential in Europe.

abdul-rahman-al-barrak.name: Abdul-Rahman al-Barrak
abdul-rahman-al-barrak.summary: Saudi Salafi cleric, born 1933 or 1934, praised by name by Osama bin Laden in 1994 for opposing the kingdom's Grand Mufti; his website was later banned for promoting bold ideas.

mihna.name: Mihna
mihna.summary: A period of religious persecution (833–851) instituted by Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun to force Sunni scholars to accept Mu'tazilite doctrine.

david-lean.name: David Lean
david-lean.summary: An English filmmaker (1908–1991) considered one of the most important figures in British cinema, director of epics such as Lawrence of Arabia and Doctor Zhivago.

t-e-lawrence.name: T. E. Lawrence
t-e-lawrence.summary: A British Army officer, archaeologist, diplomat and writer (1888–1935) famed as 'Lawrence of Arabia' for his role in the Arab Revolt against the Ottomans during World War I.

cristiano-ronaldo.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
cristiano-ronaldo.summary: Portuguese footballer (born 1985) widely regarded as one of the greatest players in history, with five Ballon d'Or awards and the record for most official career goals of any player.

neymar.name: Neymar
neymar.summary: A Brazilian professional footballer, born 1992, regarded as one of the greatest of all time and Brazil's all-time top scorer and assist provider.

sadio-man.name: Sadio Mané
sadio-man.summary: A Senegalese footballer widely regarded as one of the greatest African players, known for his years at Liverpool before joining Saudi club Al-Nassr.

jordan-henderson.name: Jordan Henderson
jordan-henderson.summary: English footballer known for leadership and versatility who captained Liverpool to the Champions League and Premier League titles before later moving abroad.

public-investment-fund.name: Public Investment Fund
public-investment-fund.summary: Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, created in 1971 and now among the world's largest with about $900 billion in assets, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

jorge-solari.name: Jorge Solari
jorge-solari.summary: Argentine former football player and manager, born in 1941.

arabian-ostrich.name: Arabian ostrich
arabian-ostrich.summary: An extinct subspecies of ostrich that lived in Arabia and the Near East until the mid-20th century, wiped out by hunting with rifles and vehicles.

jubail.name: Jubail
jubail.summary: An industrial city on Saudi Arabia's Persian Gulf coast, home to a major petrochemical industry, which grew from a small fishing village after being designated for industrial development in 1975.

arabia-modern-art-008: Accademia di Belle Arti di Roma
arabia-modern-science-001: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
arabia-modern-philosophy-002: Abu Abd al-Rahman Ibn Aqil al-Zahiri
